reason: The text depicts Moses as a leader responding to an explicitly unruly people (פרוע - without restraint) by commanding the Levites to use lethal violence against them. The action is presented with divine sanction ('Thus says the Lord, God of Israel'), and the narrative frames the violence positively as the Levites 'filling their hands to the Lord,' resulting in restored order (3,000 casualties). The divine command structure and favorable framing suggest the text endorses this approach as an appropriate leadership response to unruliness.
